newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel takes concrete steps to divide Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Israel takes concrete steps to divide Hebron.

text.p: Israeli troops, locked in almost daily clashes with Arabs, erected concrete barriers in Hebron on Sunday along an invisible line dividing the volatile West Bank city, witnesses said.
Palestinians accused the soldiers of imposing a collective punishment by isolating the 20,000 Palestinians living in Israeli-occupied Hebron from the 80,000 who live under Palestinian rule.
The soldiers are protecting the 400 Jewish settlers who live in the heart of the Israeli-controlled side.
Witnesses said no one was allowed to drive from one side to the other early on Sunday and pedestrians had to clear intensive security checks. But there were no reports of clashes.

Israel's central area commander responsible for the West Bank, Major-General Uzi Dayan, threatened to take further retaliatory action against Palestinians if they resumed throwing stones and petrol bombs.
"In a place such as Hebron, a continuation of serious events such as these will severely harm the way of life of the Palestinian population," the general told Israel Radio.

Palestinians said Israeli soldiers prevented shopkeepers from opening their stores for a fourth day as punishment for unrest sparked by hostile posters that a Jewish woman put up depicting Islam's Prophet Mohammad as a pig.
They said anti-Arab slogans calling for the evacuation of Arabs were written in Hebrew on walls and stores of the Arab area in Israeli-held Hebron.
Israel has apologised for the poster incident and the woman has been charged.

Hebron has been a scene of almost daily unrest for more than two weeks. Israeli soldiers, firing live and rubber bullets, have wounded scores of Palestinians in protests. Several soldiers have also been hurt.

Religious feelings were further inflamed when Palestinians found that Yaacoubia school was ransacked and four copies of the Koran torn up. Palestinians charged Israeli soldiers desecrated the holy books but the Israeli army denied the charge.

"Already today the trade is shut down in an important part of Hebron, we are using more force, including in the school and in the area on the city seam (the dividing line) and if the situation continues, the steps will become more severe and the way of life in this city won't be as it was," Dayan said.
Israel handed over 80 percent of Hebron to the PLO in January under a self-rule deal but kept troops behind to guard the Jewish settlers in the heart of the old city.
